newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T chief questions tobacco pact - FT.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T chief questions tobacco pact - FT.

text.p: The head of British tobacco and insurance group B.A.T Industries Plc says last week's U.S. tobacco settlement will not meet one of its key objectives, the Financial Times reported in its Thursday edition.

B.A.T chief executive Martin Broughton told the paper the pact would not achieve drastic cuts in teenage smoking, describing the targets for reductions as "unrealistic". "My expectation is that we will fail to meet them," he was reported as saying.

The FT said Broughton's comments could severely damage the changes of the White House and Congress giving their approval "by reinforcing the belief among anti-smoking groups that the settlement will benefit tobacco companies more than society".

"You must remember that this whole deal is not something we agree with," Broughton told the paper. "We don't support a lot of things that are in this package. But it is a package we are prepared to support overall in order to get a deal," he added.
The settlement calls for cigarette makers to pay $368.5 billion, some of which would be earmarked for anti-smoking and public health programmes.
